item.title: Marlins Hand Out 1,000 Meals To Miami Families On Friday
item.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports On Friday at loanDepot Park, 1,000 South Florida families received holiday meals distributed by two hundred volunteers. Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix brought his 7-month-old son to the event, according to MLB.com . The baby wore a turkey onesie while his father helped organize the distribution. This annual event marks the 18th year the team has fed local families before Thanksgiving. The team did not just drop off boxes and leave. They set up stations where families could grab turkeys, beans, rice, and stuffing mix. Volunteers also handed out pasta, tomato sauce, canned vegetables, and even protein shakes. Marlins president of business Caroline O’Connor stood at the turkey station to help. She noted that the event grows larger every single year because the team gets closer to the people. Money and Meals for Neighbors The financial support went beyond just food on a plate. Feeding South Florida was presented with a check for $48,890 as part of the initiative. This money helps the charity buy more food for the region throughout the year. About 150 Marlins employees and 50 workers from Amazon joined forces to make it happen. The group also gave out 400 extra turkeys around Miami-Dade County earlier in the week. First-time dad Bendix said the event matters deeply to his own family. “It’s such a great family event, and it’s such a great thing that we do as the Marlins to help families in the local community,” Bendix said. He added that providing for the community is a huge part of their family life. “Having our own family is something that’s really important to us, and being able to help provide for the community is a huge part of that.” Leadership and Local Support Local leaders showed up to thank the volunteers and see the work firsthand. Miami-Dade County mayor Daniella Levine Cava and City of Miami Commissioner Rolando Escalona attended the event. Escalona said the food distribution helps families who need it most. “This goes a very long way,” Escalona said, “so I’m extremely grateful for this event.” The partnership received praise from Giovanni Castro, who leads Amazon’s state and local public policy efforts. He said the team shows they are more than a ballclub. “For three years, Amazon has been a proud partner with the Marlins, and every time this team shows they’re more than a ballclub. They’re a neighbor who shows up for all of South Florida.” The story was excerpted from Christina De Nicola’s Marlins Beat newsletter.

item.title: Tottenham Must Not Waste Another Academy Prospect
item.description: Luca Williams-Barnett celebrates after scoring the first goal during the FA Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur FC and Ipswich Town FC. Credit IMAGO / Propaganda Photo Recording Date 21.11.2026 Media ID 1086192367 | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Barry Dixon, LWOF Site Manager Tottenham Hotspur have moved quickly to secure young sensation Luca Williams-Barnett’s future after the teenager signed a new contract with the club. The 18-year-old has been integrated into the first team under Roberto De Zerbi, impressing in pre-season and off the bench against Crystal Palace before making his first Premier League start against Ipswich Town, when he scored and assisted in the 2-0 win. Having joined Spurs at Under-10 level, his progression into the senior side is an example of what the academy can produce. However, Williams-Barnett’s new deal should be the beginning of a long and successful Tottenham career, rather than another case of a player slipping through the fingers of the north London club. Read More: Ipswich Performance Gives Roberto De Zerbi Selection Headaches Tottenham Must Give Williams-Barnett a Genuine First-Team Opportunity Spurs Have Struggled to Turn Potential Into First-Team Regulars Tottenham’s academy has produced some outstanding players over the years, with Harry Kane, Ledley King and Glenn Hoddle among the most famous to enjoy successful careers in north London. More recently, the likes of Kyle Walker-Peters, Harry Winks, Japhet Tanganga and Oliver Skipp all progressed through the ranks to become regular first-team players before moving to pastures new. However, it has become more difficult for Spurs to produce and retain academy graduates in recent times. Several youngsters have made their senior debuts in the last three seasons, such as Jamie Donley, Damola Ajayi, Callum Olusesi, Alfie Dorrington, Jun’ai Byfield and James Rowswell, but none have been given a real chance to show their ability in the first-team setup. Mikey Moore is another who has enjoyed a more regular involvement with the first team, especially during 2024/25, and is continuing his development out on loan, first with Rangers last season and now with FC Koln, as he hopes to add to his 22 Spurs appearances. Of course, playing young players can be a gamble and many never reach the required standard for Premier League football. However, Spurs must ensure the likes of Williams-Barnett and Moore are utilised properly with a long-term vision, rather than simply giving them the odd appearance before they seek a route out of the club. IMAGO / News Images The Ones Who Have Slipped Through the Net There are also examples of players who could have been given more of an opportunity before being allowed to leave, something Spurs must avoid if they are to get the best from their young players. item.title: Brandon Aiyuk signs in Washington, officially ending 49ers drama
item.description: The NFL future of Brandon Aiyuk has finally been decided, with the veteran wide receiver reportedly signing with the Washington Commanders following his messy departure from the San Francisco 49ers. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, Aiyuk is joining Washington’s practice squad, with his agent Drew Rosenhaus confirming the move. The signing also gives Aiyuk an opportunity to reunite with former college teammate Jayden Daniels, who is now the Commanders’ starting quarterback. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. https://t.co/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 BREAKING: Brandon Aiyuk is joining the Commanders practice squad, per his agent. The former 49ers WR is set to reunite with college teammate Jayden Daniels after clearing waivers. His offseason wishes come true. 🎥: brandonaiyuk/IG https://t.co/vM5JCJopvL — Complex Sports (@ComplexSports) November 25, 2026 The 28-year-old was released by San Francisco on Monday before passing through waivers unclaimed on Tuesday, allowing him to sign with a new organization. His departure officially brings an end to a complicated relationship with the 49ers that deteriorated over the past two seasons. MORE: Eagles’ Joe Milton details Dak Prescott’s impact on him ahead of Thanksgiving Day matchup Aiyuk’s complicated 49ers departure Dec 17, 2023; Glendale, Arizona, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk (11) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Aiyuk had originally signed a contract extension with San Francisco ahead of the 2024 season, but his campaign was cut short after suffering a torn ACL in mid-October. The wide receiver subsequently missed the entire 2025 season amid conflicting reports surrounding his health and recovery. The 49ers eventually voided his contract guarantees ahead of the 2025 campaign before placing him on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December. San Francisco general manager John Lynch appeared to acknowledge that Aiyuk’s time with the organization was finished when he addressed the situation in January 2026. “I think it’s safe to say played his last snap with the 49ers,” Lynch said. Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on November 9, giving the 49ers a two-week window to determine whether they wanted to retain him. The organization ultimately decided to release the veteran receiver. item.title: Three keys to a Gopher win over Wisconins and how to watch
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 03: Minnesota Golden Gophers defensive lineman TJ Bush Jr. (3) celebrates pressuring Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood (19) which lead to an interception during the second half to the college football game between the Michigan Wolverines and the Minnesota Golden Gophers on October 3rd, 2026, at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A Black Friday evening matchup in primetime for the 136th matchup between the Gophers and Badgers. A monumental game for both programs trying to finish the season strong. How to Watch TV: NBC Time: 6:30 Stream: Peacock PJ Fleck and the Gophers have won four of the last five matchups with Wisconsin. Can Fleck maintain his dominance over the Badgers to make it five out of six? KEYS TO A GOPHER WIN Stop all the runs – Darrion Dupree is coming off a 125-yard game at Purdue and quarterback Colton Joseph rushed for 187 yards. Stop the running backs, stop the quarterback and make Joseph pass the ball. Taking proper angles and wrapping up with solid tackling has not been a strength of this Gopher defense, but they have to find a way on Friday night. Punt returns for field position – I noticed that the Wisconsin punter has only 9 fair catches this season. For context, Tom Weston has 20. This indicates to me that punt returns will be available for Javon Tracy. Can he break one again and either give us some points or set up the offense to score? Find an offensive identity – It is the final game of the season so I realize how unlikely this is, BUT FOR GOD’S SAKE, find something to hang your hat on offensively. I do think that Drake Lindsey and whoever was calling plays got into a better rhythm in the second half last week, so maybe they’ve found a little something. And Lindsey’s two touchdown passes plus the strike to Noah Jennings down the sidelines to set up the game-winning field goal were some of the best passes he has thrown in weeks. So maybe? OPPOSING PLAYERS TO WATCH #1 QB – Colton Joseph – I am much more concerned about his legs than I am his arm. But he is the one to be most concerned with on offense. #8 LB – Mason Posa – A sophomore, coming off of a freshman All-American season. He is going to be a problem. PREDICTION I am feeling overly confident heading into this game. Wisconsin is not what they appear and I think that PJ gets unusually (yet appropriately) aggressive. Is this going to be a blowout? No chance. But are we going to shut down the Badger offense and do enough on offense to get the win? Absolutely. Minnesota – 31 Wisconsin – 17

item.title: ‘He’s finished’ – Barcelona fans continue to express concern over one player during Sabah clash
item.description: ‘He’s finished’ – Barcelona fans continue to express concern over one player during Sabah clash Supporters of La Liga giants Barcelona have on Wednesday moved to express their collective concern regarding the ongoing exploits of a member of the club’s midfield ranks. The Blaugrana star in question? Gavi. Spanish international Gavi was for his part afforded a rare opportunity to impress from the off this evening. After Barcelona made the trip to Baku to lock horns with Sabah in the Champions League, the 22-year-old was handed just his third start of the campaign. Gavi’s efforts to justify his inclusion, however, have since come up some way short… From his berth in the middle of the park, the youngster has struggled to impact the game in any meaningful manner, either going forward or whilst defending. Against one of the weaker opponents their side will meet this season, those of a Blaugrana persuasion have therefore been quick to express their collective worry about Gavi’s form. Some, in fact, have gone as far as to label the midfielder as ‘finished’. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Boston Celtics back after 131-116 NBA Cup win over Washington Wizards
item.description: The Boston Celtics are back after their 131-116 NBA Cup win over the Washington Wizards on this past Monday (Nov. 25) night. Or at least that is the point of view of the hosts of the "How Bout Them Celtics!" podcast, Jack Simone and Sam LaFrance, who took some time on a recent episode of their show to talk over how Boston snapped their four-game win streak (the longest yet of the Joe Mazzulla era) with their win vs Washington in NBA Cup action. An 80-point first half made the argument for them, but a rough third quarter did a lot of work undermining said argument. Are the Celtics really back after this won vs. the lowly wiz, or is there still plenty of work for Boston to do if they want to stay in the win column moving forward? item.title: Rams GM Makes Clear Statement on Potential WR Additions
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Rams encountered some injury trouble among their wide receivers this season, but general manager Les Snead isn’t looking to add anyone else this season. The Rams’ top two receivers in Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are out, with the former set to miss the remainder of the season after undergoing MCL surgery. Several options are open for the Rams, such as former 1,000-yard receiver Brandon Aiyuk, but Snead isn’t going to pursue anyone else. “Like I tell people all the time, it’s not Madden,” Snead said on the Coach McVay Show. “You don’t just acquire someone – in Madden, you don’t have to teach them the playbook.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by LA Sports Report (@lasportsreport) While Snead hasn’t shied away from big midseason moves in the past, acquiring players like Jalen Ramsey, Von Miller and Sony Michel with blockbuster trades in years past, he doesn’t often add to the offense midway through the season. With the deadline already behind them, any further additions for the Rams could impact their results. Nov 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams president Kevin Demoff (left), general manager Les Snead (center) and owner Stan Kroenke watch during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Who Are the Rams’ Receiving Options? Behind Nacua and Adams, the Rams’ top receiver on the season is tight end Tyler Higbee, who has less than half of Nacua’s yards and more than 150 fewer than Adams. The Rams’ next leading pass catcher is running back Kyren Williams, closely followed by Konata Mumpfield with 243 yards. Mumpfield led the Rams in receiving yards in their last game, a win against the Arizona Cardinals, logging three catches for 81 yards on the day. Veteran Tutu Atwell also figures to get more looks with Adams and Nacua sidelined, but he only caught one pass for 31 yards against the Cardinals. Who Do the Rams Play Next? Following their bye week, the Rams will face the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. PT. Both teams are 6-4, but the Rams come in with all of the momentum having won each of their last four games. The Packers and Rams both got an abbreviated bye week, lasting just 10 days rather than the standard 14, but are sure to be energized as they chase spots in the playoffs. item.title: Providence Journal soccer, volleyball poll winners announced
item.description: In the final non-football Athlete of the Week polls of the fall season, students from Tiverton, Lincoln and North Smithfield took top prizes. In Girls Volleyball, Adysson Amaral of Tiverton drew the most votes, with 1,088 votes or 50 percent of the votes cast. Amaral was dominant at the service line all night and helped the Tigers surge to an early lead in the second set. The middle blocker constantly had her hands up and made life difficult for North Providence as Tiverton finished off a 25-16, 25-14, 25-23 victory. In The Providence Journal Girls Soccer MVP poll, the winner was Brynn Santos, of North Smithfield, who garnered 3,159 votes, or 50 percent of the ballots cast. Santos was plenty dangerous for a Northmen side who remained among the contenders for a No. 1 seed into the playoff bracket. In the Boys Soccer MVP poll, Jaxon Harris, of Lincoln, took top honors, earning 1,302 votes, good for 36 percent of the ballots cast. Harris opened the door for goals off free kicks and from distance throughout the season. Our final polls of the fall season, for football player of the Super Bowls , and best highlight of the Super Bowls are active now, so be sure to cast your ballots, and congratulations again to our most recent poll winners! item.title: Insider sees a troubling path to Puka Nacua’s next Rams deal
item.description: Puka Nacua might have played his final game in a Los Angeles Rams uniform. He also might not have. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter weighed in on Nacua’s future during Tuesday’s episode of “The Adam Schefter Podcast.” “Here’s what I would say: He’s an unrestricted free agent ! And he’s an unrestricted free agent coming off a knee injury . I think they want to keep him. I think they plan to keep him. Will they actually keep him? We’ll see,” Schefter said. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter stands on the field prior to an NFL wild-card playoff football game in Houston, Saturday, Jan. 4, 2020. AP “The offseason, there’s a lot of things that come up. Puka obviously is serving a suspension now , he had off-the-field issues last offseason, now he’s got a knee injury that was operated on,” Schefter added. “He’s coming off the knee, he’s a free agent, there has been a suspension; the Rams would like him back. He’s gonna want to get paid… so how is this all gonna work out? I think it’s a mistake to say he’s not back in LA, and I think it’s a mistake to say it’s automatically [back]. We don’t know!” Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) warms up before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman Schefter believes the Rams plan to keep Nacua. Whether the two sides can agree on a price remains an open question. Losing Nacua would leave a sizable hole in the Rams’ passing game. He’s developed into one of the NFL’s best receivers in Los Angeles. Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams enters the field before a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, Nov. 1, 2026. Getty Images Los Angeles still has a season it needs to focus on, including a critical game against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. But Nacua’s contract situation will become the biggest story to follow for the Rams once their 2026-27 campaign concludes.

item.title: Badgers reclaim number one ahead of non-conference series thanks to buzzer beater
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - APRIL 11: Daniel Hauser #31 of the Wisconsin Badgers is consoled by teammates after the Denver Pioneers defeated the Wisconsin Badgers during the Division I Men's Ice Hockey Championship held at T-Mobile Arena on April 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Tyler Schank/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Super, scintillating, sensational. Dick Vitale’s three S’s came to mind watching the Wisconsin Badgers take down the Penn State Nittany Lions last weekend. They might not be the most dangerous foe in the conference right now, but they always seem to give the Badgers problems. And following their first loss against Ohio State the week before, Wisconsin could ill-afford problems. Both games were decided by just one goal, but No. 1 Wisconsin (10-1-1, 6-1-1 Big Ten) won them in very different ways, with junior Gavin Morrissey bookending the series with huge plays. We want MORRissey goals! 🍎: Finn Brink pic.twitter.com/e55Q2PW0eM — Wisconsin Hockey (@BadgerMHockey) November 21, 2026 Penn State (2-11-1, 0-7-1 Big Ten) is not having a great year, but for what it’s worth, they’ve split their last eight games with the Badgers. Morrissey fired a shot across the bow early as the Nittany Lions were on the power play Friday night. Sophomore Finn Brink chased down an errant pass off the boards in the defensive zone and slapped the puck ahead to a streaking Morrissey, who patiently handled the puck until the goaltender opened his pads and gave up the five-hole. After Penn State answered in the waning moments of the second period, it was Vasily Zelenov who cleaned up a loose rebound less than two minutes into the third period to claim the game-winning goal. Zelenov is averaging a point per game in his sophomore season and centering the second line tremendously as a key contributor, currently second on the team in assists behind only Morrissey. Saturday night is when the fireworks came into play. After Zach Wooten and JJ Wiebusch scored first-period goals sandwiched around a tally for Penn State’s Justin Poirier, the Badgers maintained their 2-1 lead for most of the game, despite bombarding the Nittany Lions to the tune of 20 shots in the second period. With just over six minutes to go, Penn State found the equalizer. It started to look like the Badgers might need overtime to try and earn the extra point and avoid a clean sweep over a team yet to win in conference play. Then chaos ensued. Things began with Gavin Morrissey winning an improbable offensive zone faceoff with ten seconds remaining. Seriously, he was horizontal and completely off his skates when he had the awareness to tap the puck back to Joe Palodichuk and move it around the horn. Palodichuk then found Hensler with a less-than-perfect pass, who corralled the puck with his skate and was barely able to redirect it toward the net. item.title: Aaron Rodgers, several Steelers ‘frustrated’ with Mike McCarthy
item.description: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The fallout of the Steelers’ decision to bench Aaron Rodgers continues as Wednesday morning turns into Wednesday afternoon. The Steelers are now getting Mason Rudolph prepared to start his first game of the season this Friday when they take on the Broncos. Amidst the whirlwind of the news, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that the relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has grown strained. “The relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has not been in a good place, and a path back together is considered ‘highly unlikely,’” Schultz reports. Additionally, it isn’t just Rodgers who has grown frustrated with McCarthy. Multiple other offensive players have, as well, according to Schultz. “The frustration is not just with Rodgers,” Schultz writes. “Multiple position groups have been upset, and I’m told McCarthy has not been what some offensive players hoped for. Frustration has been growing among everyone for weeks. The Rodgers benching is just the start of what’s being revealed publicly. I’ve also heard players who were used to having Mike Tomlin have struggled with the change.” It certainly sounds like this is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the internal frustrations and dysfunction as it pertains to this Steelers team. Don’t be surprised if more begins to come out in the coming days, Let us know what you think in the comments . item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
